1.title: Custom Detection Rules in Defender XDR
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Custom Detection Rules in Defender X D R. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Create custom detection rules by using Advanced Hunting in Microsoft Defender X D R. Manage custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender X D R. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: What a custom detection rule is
1.text: What a custom detection rule is. A custom detection rule runs an advanced hunting K Q L query on a schedule and, when it returns rows, raises an alert and can take response actions. You build the query in Advanced hunting, test it, then choose Create detection rule.

1.title: What a custom detection rule is, continued
1.text: What a custom detection rule is. The figure shows this: A hunting query becomes a scheduled rule that raises alerts and runs actions.

1.title: What a custom detection rule is, continued
1.text: What a custom detection rule is. Defender role. Security settings (manage) (unified R back). Entra roles. Security Administrator; Security Operator (if R back is off in Defender for Endpoint; if on, it also needs Manage security settings). Sentinel data. Also Microsoft Sentinel Contributor. Scope. Users also need device group permissions for the rule scope.

1.title: Query requirements
1.text: Query requirements. Time column. Timestamp (or Time Generated for Sentinel tables). Defender for Endpoint tables. Must return Device Id and Report Id. Other Defender tables. Must return Timestamp and Report Id. Impacted assets. Return identifier columns: Device Id, Device Name, Account Object Id, Account Upn, Recipient Email Address and so on. Do not. Filter on Timestamp; the service pre-filters by the lookback period. If a query uses summarize, project the columns the rule needs, because aggregation drops them. Exam tip: A rule query must return Report Id (and Device Id for endpoint tables) or it cannot be saved.

1.title: Frequency and lookback
1.text: Frequency and lookback. Every twenty-four hours. thirty days. Every twelve hours. forty-eight hours. Every three hours. twelve hours. Every hour. four hours. Continuous (N R T). Near real time. Custom. Sentinel-only data; five minutes to fourteen days. On save, the rule checks the past thirty days. Continuous (N R T) rules need a query on one table only: no joins, no unions, no externaldata, and no comment lines. Supported tables include Device Events, Device Process Events, Email Events, Identity Logon Events, Cloud App Events, Alert Evidence.

1.title: Frequency and lookback, continued
1.text: Frequency and lookback. Alerts per rule per run. one hundred fifty. Custom details. twenty key-value pairs, four kilobytes combined per alert. Dynamic title or description. three columns per field. Exam tip: Fastest detection equals Continuous (N R T), but one table, no joins. If you need a join, use hourly or slower.

1.title: Alert details and scope
1.text: Alert details and scope. You set the alert title, severity, category, my ter techniques, description and recommended actions; the impacted entities (device, user, mailbox) come from the query columns. Scope: All devices or Specific device groups (this affects only device-based rules).

1.title: Response actions
1.text: Response actions. Device. Actions: Isolate device, Collect investigation package, Run antivirus scan, Initiate investigation, Restrict app execution. Needs: Device Id. File. Actions: Allow or Block; Quarantine file. Needs: A file I D such as S H A one or S H A two hundred fifty-six; Remediate permission. User. Actions: Mark user as compromised (sets Entra risk to high); Disable user; Reset user authentication. Needs: Account Object Id; S I D columns for disable and reset.

1.title: Response actions, continued
1.text: Response actions. Email. Actions: Move to mailbox folder (Junk, Inbox, Deleted items); Delete email (Soft delete or Hard delete). Needs: Network Message Id and Recipient Email Address. Exam tip: Actions need the right columns. A user action needs an account identifier; an email action needs Network Message Id and Recipient Email Address.

1.title: Managing rules
1.text: Managing rules. Path: Hunting, then Custom detection rules. List columns. Last run, Last run status, Next run, Status. Rule page. Run, Edit, Modify query, Turn on or Turn off, Delete (deleting turns the rule off and removes it permanently), Include or exclude from correlation. Sections. Triggered alerts and Triggered actions. Custom detection alerts join the incident queue and are correlated with other alerts, unless the rule is excluded from correlation.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A sock wants a detection that fires within minutes of a suspicious process starting on endpoints. Which frequency fits, and what is the limit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Continuous (N R T), with a query on a single table without joins. Continuous (N R T) runs in near real time but allows only one table and no joins or unions.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An analyst writes a hunting query for Device Process Events with summarize and tries to create a rule, but saving fails. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The query does not return the required Device Id and Report Id columns. Endpoint rule queries must return Device Id and Report Id; summarize can drop them.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A user must create custom detection rules in Defender X D R with the least privilege and no Sentinel data. Which permission fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Security settings (manage), or Security Administrator in Entra. Creating rules needs Security settings (manage) or the Security Administrator role.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A rule must disable a user account when it fires. Which column requirement applies? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The query must return the account S I D columns. Disable user and reset authentication need S I D columns in addition to the account identifier.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A rule returns four hundred matching rows in one run. How many alerts does the rule generate for that run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: one hundred fifty alerts, the limit per rule per run. A rule generates at most one hundred fifty alerts per run.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A rule runs every twenty-four hours. How much Defender X D R data does each run look back over? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The last thirty days of data. A twenty-four-hour frequency uses a thirty-day lookback; twelve hours uses forty-eight hours, three hours uses twelve hours and hourly uses four hours.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Where are custom detection rules managed? Answer: Hunting, then Custom detection rules. Question two. What is the maximum number of alerts per rule per run? Answer: one hundred fifty. Question three. Which frequency is near real time? Answer: Continuous (N R T).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which columns must endpoint rule queries return? Answer: Device Id and Report Id (with a timestamp). Question five. Which file actions can a rule take? Answer: Allow or block, and quarantine file. Question six. What happens when you delete a rule? Answer: It is turned off and removed permanently.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Permission: Security settings (manage); Security Administrator. Query: Timestamp, Report Id, Device Id (endpoint tables). Frequency: twenty-four h equals thirty days; twelve h equals forty-eight h; three h equals twelve h. N R T: one table, no joins, no unions, no comments. Limits: one hundred fifty alerts per run; twenty custom details, four kilobytes. Actions: device, file, user, email.
